title: Tendon
description: A named tendon: the fibrous continuation of one or more muscles onto bone (or, for a small number of intra-articular tendons, directly onto a labrum/joint capsule). Most muscles' tendinous attachment is already fully described by muscle.schema.json's attachments.insertion_bone/insertion_landmark and is NOT duplicated here -- this schema exists for tendons with genuine standalone identity beyond 'the insertion of one simple muscle': multiple muscles converging into one conjoined/conjoint tendon (pes anserinus, the hamstrings' proximal conjoint origin, the abdominal conjoint tendon), a tendon with documented internal layering (the quadriceps tendon's 3 fiber layers, the Achilles tendon's spiraling gastrocnemius/soleus fiber contributions), a fibro-osseous pulley/sheath system (the finger flexor tendons' annular/cruciate pulleys), or a clinically-named region distinct from simple muscle anatomy (the rotator cuff's hypovascular 'critical zone', the common flexor/extensor tendon origins of 'golfer's'/'tennis' elbow). Modeled with the same 'one-or-more functionally distinct pieces per named structure' convention as muscle's functional_compartments, ligament's bands, and cartilage's parts.

tendon_type.description: simple_cord: a single round/cordlike tendon (Achilles); flat_aponeurotic: a broad flat sheet (quadriceps tendon, extensor hood); conjoined_multi_muscle: two or more distinct muscles' tendons fusing into one shared structure (pes anserinus, conjoint tendon); fibrous_sheath_pulley_system: a tendon running through a retinacular/pulley tunnel system (finger flexor tendons + their annular/cruciate pulleys); intra_articular: a tendon segment running within a joint capsule before reaching its bony attachment (biceps brachii long head).

parent_muscles.description: ids of the muscle(s) (schema/muscle.schema.json) this tendon is the fibrous continuation of -- more than one entry for a conjoined tendon.

attachments.description: Overall span: where the tendon leaves its parent muscle(s) and where it ends on bone (or, for intra_articular tendons, its bony/labral origin and its eventual bony insertion).

ref.description: muscle id or bone id, matching 'type'

retinaculum_or_pulley_refs.description: ids of related fibrous_sheath_pulley/retinaculum entries in schema/fascia.schema.json data, if this tendon runs through one.

parts.description: Anatomically/functionally distinct components of this one named tendon (e.g. the quadriceps tendon's 3 fiber layers, the pes anserinus's 3 muscle contributions, the rotator cuff tendon complex's 4 tendons). A tendon with no meaningful internal subdivision still gets exactly one parts[] entry.

parent_muscle.description: the specific muscle this part continues from, for multi-part/conjoined tendons

failure_load_N.description: representative literature ultimate tensile load, where documented -- an illustrative typical value, not a patient-specific measurement (see docs/SOURCES.md's representative-vs-exact-values policy).
